component.name: Airloom
component.summary: See the air around you, sensor by sensor

description.p: Airloom is a focused air-quality map for the GNOME desktop. It presents nearby public PurpleAir readings, recent trends, favorites, and local AQI threshold alerts in a clean, native interface.
Airloom includes a clearly labeled demo mode and accepts a personal PurpleAir read key for live data.
Fixed: downloaded Flatpak bundles failed to install with a GPG verification error — release bundles are now properly signed.

Fixed: saving preferences no longer jumps the sensor data back to your home area while you are browsing somewhere else on the map — saves now refresh the area you are looking at. Choosing a new fixed home still moves the map there.

Sensors with poor agreement between their two laser channels (PurpleAir confidence below 90 percent) are now hidden by default, with a new Hide low-confidence sensors preference to show them again; sensors without a confidence score stay visible. The local sensor cache is now schema-versioned and clears itself once on upgrade so every cached reading carries the new field.

Live PurpleAir data is now cached locally, cutting API credit usage dramatically: map areas are reused within a configurable refresh interval (new Refresh interval preference, default 2 minutes), repeat polls fetch only sensors that changed, trend charts load per sensor on demand, and very wide map views cap the fetched area. The header refresh button always forces a fresh poll, and if PurpleAir is unreachable your cached readings are shown instead of demo data.

Sensors can now be hidden (for erroneous units) via eye-off buttons on the detail pane and map popup; a new Preferences section lists hidden sensors with per-sensor Unhide and Unhide all. Hidden sensors are excluded everywhere, including alerts; favorites keep their star across hide and unhide.
Airloom now presents itself as a GNOME desktop app rather than Fedora-only: the Flatpak runs on any Linux distribution with the GNOME runtime. No functional changes.
No application changes; confirms the automatic-update pipeline end to end.
Installed copies now update automatically through a signed Flatpak repository; new bundles come preconfigured with it as their update source.

Zooming out past a configurable distance now merges the sensor dots into a heat map of interpolated air quality; zooming back in restores the individual markers. A new "Heat map beyond (km)" preference controls the switch point.
The close button on the sensor detail card is larger and easier to see.
Hardening release: development debugging support is now fully excluded from installed builds.
Trackpad pinch now zooms the map around your fingers instead of scaling the whole window: the gesture is intercepted before the web engine can apply its internal page zoom.
Clicking a sensor marker now reliably opens its popup: pointer releases no longer rebuild the marker layer before the click is delivered.

Map zoom is now smoothly animated and anchored under the cursor, trackpad pinch zooms the map instead of breaking the interface, sensor markers open a compact popup with a link to the PurpleAir web map, and a new map chip filters outdoor, indoor, or all sensors.
Place-search navigation now shows the sensors at the destination instead of leaving the map empty, and the area AQI chip is labeled with the area currently in view rather than always showing home.

Location detection now works on first launch: the permission request waits for the app window to gain focus so GNOME's location dialog can appear, a fix arriving after the detection timeout is still applied, and a failed first-run detection is reported honestly instead of showing the default area as a known location.
Small towns are now labeled by name rather than by their county.
Location detection now distinguishes precise fixes from coarse IP-level guesses and never overwrites a known location with the wrong city.
Automatic location detection, place search, and redesigned map-first interface with persistent tile rendering and independent alert timers.
Hardening release: resilient refreshes, safer external-link handling, private config storage, the full piecewise EPA smoke correction, and automatic background refresh for alerts.
Initial Fedora MVP.
